source.title: Geometric Similarity in VLM Low-Level Vision Representations
source.authors: Shao-Jun Xia; Huixin Zhang; Zhen Lei; Anlan Sun; Yuner Zhang; Xiaoyang Chen

record.tranche_reason: The study measures cross-model representational geometry using dCor, nearest-neighbor overlap, Procrustes residuals, and SAE activation-rate MMD. These are conceptual tests of cross-model alignment, but the study does not reproduce a scale-and-capability trend.
record.gate_note: The study compares seven models across 21 model pairs on low-level vision tasks, but does not test whether alignment increases with model size or capability. It does not evaluate paired image-caption alignment, shared features across seeds, or stitching and unpaired mapping. Cited results from other studies are not included as rows. Within-model task organization and other results that do not measure cross-model alignment are omitted.
record.test_reason: The study measures same-task cross-model alignment across 21 pairs of seven VLMs, using dCor, Huh et al.'s mutual-kNN overlap and held-out orthogonal Procrustes. The setting is new: the representations are task-minus-neutral-prompt displacements for 24 low-level vision tasks. The results bear on how complete and metric-dependent convergence is (V6, V7) and on linear interchangeability (V4). They do not relate alignment to scale, so V1's trend is untested. T3 fits better than T2 because the representation type and domain differ from the originals, not only the method.
record.authors_conclusion: Broadly right. The authors conclude that cross-model universality is substantial but limited. It is mainly global relational geometry (similar distance structure), not local neighborhoods, a shared coordinate frame, or pointwise feature correspondence. They add that feature-level sharing via SAEs needs explicit cross-model validation, and that within-model task structure is mechanism-centric rather than family-centric.
record.recipe_differences: Uses a four-level analysis of task-conditioned low-level vision representations across models, with dCor, NNGS, held-out Procrustes alignment, SAE activation-rate MMD, and supplementary topology. It does not test a scale-and-capability trend.
record.method_sensitivity: The choice of geometric measure changes the apparent strength of cross-model agreement: dCor is higher than chance-adjusted NNGS, while held-out PAR exceeds its mean-prediction baseline for most model pairs. NNGS uses k=10.

fits_no_version.finding: Same-task cross-model SAE activation-rate MMD falls below the within-model different-task reference for only 6 of 21 pairs (3 across all seeds).
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Models trained independently show similar distributions of sparse-feature usage for the same input task.

fits_no_version.finding: The per-task LID ordering is consistent across seven models (mean Spearman ρ=0.80; Denoising lowest in all). Cross-model disagreement in task-similarity structure (0.71 SD) exceeds the gap between task families.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Second-order geometric properties of task representations, such as intrinsic dimensionality ordering, are shared across architectures.

record.problems: No scale or capability trend is measured; the model set spans only two stated size groupings and results are aggregated over model pairs. Only one selected layer per model is analyzed for the single-layer comparisons. The authors note that standardized prompts, a transformer-dominated model set, task-specific dataset differences, and the projection and SAE choices may limit generalization or require further validation.
record.rows_left_out: Omitted within-model instruction-displacement cosine and LID results, within-model task-pair organization, and cross-task/model rankings because they do not directly measure the claim versions retained here. Supplementary topological distances are shown for selected pair-task combinations but do not provide a stated scalar summary establishing interchangeable representations or a scale trend.

untested.parts: No relation of alignment to model size or capability. Base (~7–8B) and large (>13B) groups exist but are not compared.
No image–caption or vision–language paired alignment.
No models retrained from different seeds. SAE seeds are not model seeds.
Stitching, general linear maps, relative representations and unpaired mapping are not tested. Only held-out orthogonal Procrustes is.
No matching of individual features or circuits across models.
No sweep over metric settings such as k. No out-of-distribution inputs. Only one layer per model.
No test of plateau with scale, and none of whether shared data or objectives explain alignment.

missing.what: Correlation of task mean LID with cross-model agreement: ρ=+0.853 with PAR and ρ=−0.764 with NNGS. Every task with LID >15 has PAR >1.1. This shows convergence depends on the inputs and task.
Per-pair dCor, NNGS, PAR and topology values, ordered by dCor (Figure 4). These could allow a base-vs-large comparison, but no numbers are stated in the text.

record.verdict_notes: The representations are differences between last-token states under a task prompt and a neutral prompt; for Qwen-Image-Edit they are DiT condition-feature means. They are not standard image embeddings, which limits direct comparison with the Platonic Representation Hypothesis. NNGS follows Huh et al. (k=10, chance-adjusted). Only one stable layer per model is analyzed, and different tasks draw on different datasets. The reader's V4 label for r4 was removed because MMD fits no map. No scale analysis is present, so V1 receives no verdict.

versions.untested_parts: No alignment trend across model size or capability is reported; pairwise cross-model results are aggregated rather than related to scale or performance.
No paired image-caption or vision-language cross-modal alignment comparison.
No comparison of networks trained from different initializations for shared features or subspaces. SAE seeds are not model-training seeds.
Tests held-out orthogonal Procrustes alignment only; does not test stitching, relative representations, arbitrary linear maps, or mapping without paired data.
SAE activation-rate distributions are compared, but individual features are not matched across models, so recurrence of the same interpretable features or circuits is not tested.
Shows different outcomes across global, local, and alignment metrics. Does not vary the input distribution or test out-of-distribution data, and does not report a sweep over metric settings.
Reports incomplete global/local and coordinate alignment. Does not test whether alignment plateaus with scale or whether shared training data or objectives explain the results.

rows.check: A chance-adjusted NNGS of 0.27 against global dCor of 0.77 is what V7 (far from complete) and V6 (metric dependence) describe. The state should be observed, not partial. Only k=10 was used, so this is no sweep over settings.

rows.subject: 21 model pairs (all seven models)

rows.operation_detail: Fit an orthogonal Procrustes map on 80% of rows and evaluated normalized residual on held-out rows.
rows.value: mean residual = 1.049; 16 of 21 pairs scored above 1.0
rows.note: The text says the fitted orthogonal alignment fails to generalize to held-out data overall. Five pairs were not above the stated baseline.
rows.check: The state refers to V4: a held-out orthogonal map does no better than predicting the mean (1.049; 16/21 pairs >1.0). For V6 and V7 the same number is consistent with the challenge. Only an orthogonal map on 64 PCA dimensions was tested, not a general linear map.

rows.measure: Same-task cross-model activation-rate MMD relative to matched within-model, different-task MMD

rows.check: SAE activation-rate MMD compares unordered distributions of feature usage. It fits no map (V4) and matches no features (V5). The authors say it does not establish feature correspondence. Move it to fits_no_version.
